# Accounts and repositories {#sec-accounts}

Your portfolio can be a place where you show not only your data science projects, but also where people can learn where else to reach you and keep up with your work.

Here are a few key social links to keep on your portfolio website, and prerequisites that will be useful for all of these accounts (your headshot and bio):

## Headshot

Your headshot is a photo of you for a professional audience!

Jump to [2.1 and 2.2 Headshot and Bio](_2a-headshot-and-2b-bio#sec-headshot)

## Short bio

Your bio is a description of who you are, your interests, accolades, and experience. The length will vary depending on the context. The tips in this guide will be tailored for these online platforms.

Jump to [2.1 and 2.2 Headshot and Bio](_2a-headshot-and-2b-bio#sec-bio)

## GitHub

We're using GitHub a ton in our DataTrail class. As you continue to work on data science projects, your GitHub profile can be a great artifact of your work.

Jump to [2.3 GitHub](_2c-github.qmd#sec-github)

## CV

Your curriculum vitae, or CV, will be very similar to the familiar resume. It is allowed to be longer (some senior professionals have high double-digit CVs...) and document a fuller history of your academic, research, and professional accomplishments.

Jump to [2.4 CV](_2d-cv.qmd#sec-cv)

## LinkedIn

LinkedIn is a professional social media network. Your profile has sections for specific types of professional accomplishments. You'll use LinkedIn to connect with other professionals.

Jump to [2.5 LinkedIn](_2e-linkedin.qmd#sec-linkedin)

## Kaggle

Kaggle is a data science website that hosts datasets and competitions. You'll soon be acclimated with Kaggle via DataTrail competitions!

Jump to [2.6 Kaggle](_2f-kaggle.qmd#sec-kaggle)
